The flow starts in [`src/app/(auth)/login/login-form.tsx`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/43472a71-881a-4cfc-83c6-28846da5b45a/src/app/(auth)/login/login-form.tsx). The form validates the email and password with `loginSchema`, then calls the server action `loginAction`. That schema runs again on the server in [`src/actions/auth/login.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/43472a71-881a-4cfc-83c6-28846da5b45a/src/actions/auth/login.ts). Before checking credentials, `loginAction` charges the attempt to an anonymous rate-limit bucket. `auth-service.ts` also applies a login rate limit; it looks up the email, retrieves the stored password hash, and calls `verifyPassword`. In [`src/lib/hash.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/43472a71-881a-4cfc-83c6-28846da5b45a/src/lib/hash.ts), that derives a scrypt key from the submitted password and compares it to the saved key with a timing-safe comparison. Unknown email and wrong password produce the same credentials error. The user lookup and password-hash accessor are `findUserByEmail` and `findPasswordHash` in [`src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/43472a71-881a-4cfc-83c6-28846da5b45a/src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts).

On success, `auth-service.login` calls `createSessionToken` in [`src/server/services/session-service.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/43472a71-881a-4cfc-83c6-28846da5b45a/src/server/services/session-service.ts). It generates a random 32-byte token, sets a 30-day expiry, hashes the token with SHA-256, and stores that hash in a session row. [`src/server/repositories/session-repository.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/43472a71-881a-4cfc-83c6-28846da5b45a/src/server/repositories/session-repository.ts) stores the hash alongside the user ID, expiry, and nullable active organization ID. The raw token is not stored in the database. `loginAction` resolves the new token to a `SessionPrincipal` and calls `setSessionCookie` in [`src/lib/session.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/43472a71-881a-4cfc-83c6-28846da5b45a/src/lib/session.ts). The browser receives the raw token only as the `taskflow_session` cookie, marked `httpOnly`, `sameSite: "lax"`, and `secure` in production. The action result also returns the `SessionPrincipal`—user ID, email, active organization ID, and expiry—but never the token. The “Keep me signed in” checkbox is parsed, but the session service currently uses the same 30-day lifetime either way.

When the action succeeds, the login form navigates to its `next` destination, defaulting to `/orgs`; [`src/app/(dashboard)/orgs/page.tsx`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/43472a71-881a-4cfc-83c6-28846da5b45a/src/app/(dashboard)/orgs/page.tsx) redirects users with one organization straight to its slug route. On a later request, [`src/proxy.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/43472a71-881a-4cfc-83c6-28846da5b45a/src/proxy.ts) checks whether the cookie exists and redirects cookie-less requests to login. That check is only a quick gate: it does not query the database or prove the session is valid.

The actual signed-in check is `getSessionPrincipal` in `src/lib/session.ts`. It reads the cookie, hashes its token, and calls `resolveSession`; the repository looks up the matching session and returns `null` if it is missing or expired. `getSessionPrincipal` also checks the returned expiry against the current time. The dashboard root layout uses this result to redirect unauthenticated users, while the org chooser and tenant layout also require a principal. The API endpoint [`src/app/api/auth/session/route.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/43472a71-881a-4cfc-83c6-28846da5b45a/src/app/api/auth/session/route.ts) uses the same check when a client needs to re-check a session; it returns principal fields, never the cookie token.

A `SessionPrincipal` identifies the user but has no role. In the tenant layout, [`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/layout.tsx`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/43472a71-881a-4cfc-83c6-28846da5b45a/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/layout.tsx) passes that principal and the URL’s organization slug to `resolveActorForOrg`. In `session-service.ts`, that resolves the organization, looks up the user’s membership, requires it to be active, and builds an `Actor` containing `userId`, `orgId`, and the membership’s role. It checks the tenant scope and updates `lastSeenAt`. If the organization or active membership is missing, the layout returns a not-found response.

The tenant layout builds a feature-flag snapshot and passes the `Actor` into `DashboardShell` in [`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/_components/dashboard-shell.tsx`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/43472a71-881a-4cfc-83c6-28846da5b45a/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/_components/dashboard-shell.tsx). `AppSidebar` in [`src/components/domain/nav/app-sidebar.tsx`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/43472a71-881a-4cfc-83c6-28846da5b45a/src/components/domain/nav/app-sidebar.tsx) calls `visibleNav` from [`src/config/nav.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/43472a71-881a-4cfc-83c6-28846da5b45a/src/config/nav.ts). For each declared navigation item, `visibleNav` checks its required action with `can()` and any required feature flag. `can()` in [`src/lib/permissions.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/43472a71-881a-4cfc-83c6-28846da5b45a/src/lib/permissions.ts) checks tenant scope and the role matrix (with ownership rules where applicable). The resulting filtered navigation is what makes the sidebar reflect the user’s role and organization.
